name: motor
description: DC motor driver via H-bridge (L298N, TB6612FNG). Controls speed (-1.0 reverse to +1.0 forward) and direction using two GPIO pins for IN1/IN2.

constructor_params.name: direction
constructor_params.description: 1=normal, -1=reverse (for correcting reverse wiring without changing logic)

constructor_params.name: max_duty
constructor_params.description: Max duty value (1023 for ESP32, 65535 for RP2040)

properties.name: speed
properties.description: Current speed -1.0~+1.0. Setting auto-applies to PWM.

example:
from machine import Pin
from motor import Motor
import time

motor = Motor(Pin(14), Pin(15))
motor.speed = 0.7
time.sleep(2)
motor.speed = -0.5
time.sleep(2)
motor.stop()
motor.deinit()
esp32_notes: Speed is clamped to [-1.0, +1.0] — values outside are clipped
speed=0 sets both PWM channels to 0 (coast mode, not brake)
direction=-1 swaps the meaning: positive speed drives the other physical direction
hardware_notes: MUST use external H-bridge (L298N, TB6612FNG). Never connect motors directly to GPIO.
Motor power supply must be separate (NOT 3.3V/5V from dev board)
Voltage must match motor rating (e.g., 6V motor = 6V supply)
Higher PWM frequency (5-10kHz) reduces audible motor whine
differences_from_standard_mp: Standard MicroPython requires manual PWM control of two pins with direction logic. Motor wraps this.
Speed normalized to -1.0~+1.0 regardless of max_duty — easier mental model
